response:
Reflection: the full-universe zero-R&D convention is now confirmed as the backbone — all six gen-7 signals cleared 4.8% alpha with t≥3.66 at 0.141 coverage. Two refinements improved on the base independently: **netting goodwill out of the intangible-intensity leg** gave the best reliability and Sharpe (5.7%, t=4.92, Sharpe 0.485), and the **gross-profitability overlay** gave the best alpha and by far the best cross-sectional slope (5.9%, t=4.45, fmb 6.39). The cash-preferred value leg raised the FMB slope to 5.80 with Sharpe 0.459, while PlainYield showed the R&D add-back in the numerator contributes almost nothing (5.4%, t=4.44) — the work is done by knowledge intensity and by the composition/quality screens. With two generations left I now combine the independently validated refinements, broaden the intangible stock to include advertising, and test one structurally different aggregator.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: FullUniverse_NetKnowledge_Profitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3))), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing is strongest for cheap firms whose intangible capital is internally built rather than acquired and whose operations are genuinely profitable; combining the goodwill-netted intensity leg with gross profitability should deliver both the largest alpha and the strongest cross-sectional slope.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: These are the two refinements that each improved the full-universe base on different metrics — goodwill netting on reliability and Sharpe (t=4.92, 0.485), profitability on alpha and FMB slope (5.9%, fmb 6.39) — and they address distinct sources of long-leg contamination (overpaid acquirers versus unprofitable shells). Their information should be complementary rather than redundant.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: FullUniverse_CashYield_NetKnowledge
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ib), COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-based cheapness avoids the amortization and write-off distortions that goodwill-heavy firms create in earnings, so pairing it with a goodwill-netted intangible-intensity leg attacks the same accounting distortion from both the income-statement and balance-sheet sides.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The cash-preferred value leg produced the second-highest FMB slope (5.80) and Sharpe 0.459, while goodwill netting produced the highest alpha t-stat, and the two are economically aligned because acquisition accounting depresses earnings but not cash flow. This tests whether combining them removes the residual noise that keeps the base signal's FMB slope near 4.4.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: FullUniverse_NetKnowledge_DualScaled
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3)), RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Net internally generated intangible capital should be measured against both revenue and assets, because the two scalers misclassify different firms; averaging them gives the most robust ranking of the accounting-conservatism gap across the full universe.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Dual scaling and goodwill netting are orthogonal design choices that each held or improved the base result, and dual scaling matters more in the full universe where the mass of zero-R&D firms makes any single scaler's ordering coarse. This isolates whether measurement robustness or the profitability screen is the better use of the second rank slot.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: FullUniverse_TotalIntangibleSpendStock
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(TS_SUM(xad, 5), SUB(at, at))), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Advertising builds brand capital that accounting expenses exactly as it does R&D, so the economically correct hidden-asset stock is cumulative R&D plus cumulative advertising net of goodwill; including advertising should extend the mechanism to consumer-facing firms currently ranked as non-innovators.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every signal so far measures intangible capital only through R&D, which mechanically assigns zero hidden capital to brand-intensive retailers and consumer firms that spend heavily on advertising — a large part of the full universe now included by the zero convention. The earlier standalone advertising signal failed, but it used an advertising-turnover leg and a narrow sample, whereas here advertising simply completes the intangible stock inside the winning frame.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: FullUniverse_CashNetKnowledge_Profitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ib), COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3))), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))
HYPOTHESIS: The fully specified mechanism is cash-based cheapness, internally built intangible intensity, and demonstrated operating profitability acting together; each element removes a distinct source of misclassification, so the joint signal should be the most reliable expression of the value-times-intangibles interaction.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the maximal combination of the three components that improved on the full-universe base, and the archive shows that three-channel stacking only diluted results when the added channel was weakly evidenced (revenue growth, internal funding) — here all three are individually strong at 0.141 coverage. It is the natural candidate for the final recommended signal if it dominates on both alpha t-stat and FMB slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Conjunctive_CheapAndKnowledgeIntensive
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing requires both conditions simultaneously — a firm must be cheap *and* intangible-intensive — so a conjunctive aggregator that scores a firm by its weaker rank should isolate the interaction more cleanly than an additive average, which lets an extreme on one dimension substitute for the other.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every strong archive signal uses additive rank aggregation, which by construction admits firms that are merely very cheap or merely very research-intensive, so the current long leg is not a pure interaction portfolio. Taking the minimum of the two ranks is a structurally different aggregator that enforces the joint condition and, unlike the multiplicative signed forms that failed earlier, keeps both inputs monotone and bounded.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
